scalar_boundaries.nonstrict_integer_comparison: For integer k, k>=theta iff k>=ceil(theta).

scalar_boundaries.interpretation: Coefficient, integer rounding and threshold equality are distinct semantics. No microscopic spike behavior or SNN performance is inferred.

directed_decay_rounding.kind: Closed-form scalar code arithmetic, not a neural simulation
directed_decay_rounding.value_lineage: C27/P63 preserves meaningful decay progress; C28/P65 compares faithful numerical representations under H70—H74.
assumptions: Nonnegative uniform codes k=0..K for a scalar on[0,1], initially at full scale.
Isolated multiplication by a with0<a<1 before destination rounding; no graph, input, noise, transfer, cancellation, phase field or retained residual.
The comparison concerns nearest ties-to-even versus floor of the updated positive value. Coefficient/intermediate storage precision is a separate issue.
A stored zero is a numerical boundary here, not an adopted natural-cessation criterion.

identities.finite_bound: Every positive code falls by at least one, so zero occurs in at most k_initial frames for any fixed0<a<1.
identities.one_code_condition: If0<(1-a)*K<1, every positive code falls by exactly one.
identities.nearest_freeze_condition: If(1-a)*K<1/2, every code is unchanged by nearest rounding; no tie occurs.

reference.calculation: 80-digit Decimal exp/ln verifies the inequality with a wide margin; frame counts then follow exactly without stepping a trajectory.

cases.nearest_writeback: Every code is a fixed point because its decrement is strictly below half a code.
cases.floor_writeback: Every positive code decreases by exactly one per operation.
